policies.description: Before invoking **update_location**, the assistant must verify that the requesting user has a confirmed role that is authorized to perform update operations.
references: First you must check the user information and operate exclusively based on confirmed user roles, verified record relationships, and ITIL/database integrity rules.

policies.description: Any request to update a location must include all mandatory fields: the **location_id** (required) and at least one other field to be changed.
references: Mandatory Fields: Any request to create or update a record must validate all mandatory fields.

policies.description: If a required field for **update_location** is missing, the assistant must report which field is required instead of asking the user for more information.
references: User Clarification: Do not ask for further information. If the request is ambiguous, return the list and state the ambiguity. If a mandatory field is missing, state which field is required.

policies.description: The location update must be performed as a single validated operation; the assistant must not proceed if required data is missing or if the current record state prevents the update.
references: Atomic Operations: Perform one validated operation at a time, except when using approved batch endpoints. Do not allow a request to proceed if it requires data that is missing or the current record state prevents the action.

policies.description: Before updating, the assistant must verify that the specified **location_id** exists by performing a lookup; it must not assume the identifier is valid.
references: When identifiers such as names or IDs are missing, perform lookups, verify that you are reusing correct values from previous responses, and proceed using the retrieved data.

policies.policy_name: No Assumption of IDs or Outcomes
policies.description: The assistant must rely only on verified API results when updating a location and must not fabricate IDs, responses, or outcomes.
references: Never assume or fabricate IDs, responses, or outcomes — rely solely on verified API results. The same is the case of optional or default arguments.
